outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) The interface uses the label “Popularity” (sort=byPopularity) rather than an explicit “Points” sort; as long as the visible ordering is points-descending, this naming difference is not material. (2) The agent didn’t (and seemingly couldn’t) explicitly cite the browser’s current date; using the built-in “Past Year” filter is a reasonable way to satisfy the one-year window requirement.

Critical issues: None found in the final verified state. The latest DOM-model (state 5) explicitly confirms the required query and filters are applied: URL includes query=LLM, dateRange=pastYear, and type=show_hn, and the on-page controls show “Past Year” and “Show HN” active. Sorting is shown as “Popularity”/sort=byPopularity, and the visible top results in that final filtered view show point totals in descending order (915, 537, 495), supporting the agent’s claim that the list is sorted by points-descending within this UI. The agent’s reported top three results (titles, points, comment counts) exactly match DOM state 5: (1) “Show HN: I built a tiny LLM to demystify how language models work” — 915 points, 134 comments; (2) “Show HN: Needle2: 14MB agentic LLM for phones, wearables, smart home and robots” — 537 points, 185 comments; (3) “Show HN: How I topped the HuggingFace open LLM leaderboard on two gaming GPUs” — 495 points, 126 comments. Constraints were respected (no sign-in, no voting/commenting/submitting actions), and the agent stopped after reaching a state that verifies query + filters + sort + the top 3 results.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to use Algolia’s Hacker News search to find the top 3 ‘LLM’ results restricted to Show HN posts from the past year, sorted by points, and report each item’s title, points, and comment count. A reasonable user would be flexible about whether the UI calls the sort “Points” versus “Popularity” as long as it demonstrably yields a points-descending order, but would not be flexible about wrong filters (not actually Show HN / not past year) or incorrect top-3 items/metrics.
